property_summary: After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum equals the value set during initialization.
MinSum never decreases.
After calling SetMinSum with a value and then calling Initialized, MinSum returns the initial value set before Initialized.
After Collect(uint256) is called, MinSum is unchanged (equals the initial MinSum set before Initialized).
After a call to Collect, the MinSum value stored in the contract equals the value set by the last SetMinSum call, even if Initialized has been called.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum remains unchanged from its initial value.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, MinSum remains equal to its initial value (which is 0 after deployment, and SetMinSum reverts when not initialized).
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), calling SetMinSum(0) does not revert.
After a call to Collect that successfully updates balance, MinSum is either unchanged from its previous value or was changed by a prior successful SetMinSum call.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum remains 0.
Calling SetMinSum after Initialized should not change MinSum.
After Collect reverts, MinSum stays unchanged from its value before the call.
After a successful Collect call, MinSum must not change.
After Collect is called, MinSum must equal the value set in SetMinSum before Initialized.
The MinSum state variable must remain unchanged after any call to Collect, regardless of the input parameters.
After calling Collect, the value of LogFile remains equal to its value before the call because SetLogFile has no effect.
After calling Collect with any amount, the LogFile state variable should remain unchanged from its initial zero address.
LogFile address is zero after Collect if SetLogFile was never called
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the LogFile address must not be zero.
After any valid Collect call, the LogFile address should be set (non-zero) if SetLogFile was previously called successfully.
The Collect function only updates the LogFile when the call succeeds, and the LogFile address is set by SetLogFile.
After calling Collect, c.SetLogFile() is never the zero address.
After calling Collect, the LogFile address is always equal to the address set by the most recent successful SetLogFile call.
After any Collect call that does not revert, c.SetLogFile() must be zero address (due to the bug). The reference contract ensures it is non-zero.
After any successful Collect call, c.SetLogFile() must return a non-zero address.

After Collect(uint256) is called with a valid amount, the balance of the caller should never increase (it should only decrease or stay the same) because Collect only transfers funds out if conditions are met.
After calling Collect with a valid amount, the caller's balance must never exceed the sum of its initial balance and the amount it attempted to collect.

After a Collect call that does not revert, the unlockTime of the caller should strictly increase or stay the same (not decrease), because updating lockTime only when block.timestamp+_lockTime > unlockTime prevents setting a later time after an earlier one.
After a Collect call that does not revert, the unlockTime of the caller should never be less than what it was before the call.
After Collect(uint256) is called, the unlockTime of the caller should strictly increase when the lock time is updated, otherwise it should stay the same.
After a call to Collect, the unlockTime of the caller's Holder is at least the block timestamp minus the lockTime parameter.
The balance of the contract after Collect is always at least the sum of all callers' unlockTime values.
After calling Collect with a given amount, the contract's ether balance decreases exactly by that amount when the call succeeds.
After a call to Collect, the msg.sender's unlockTime is strictly greater than block.timestamp minus _lockTime when the caller's balance meets the conditions.
After a call to Collect that succeeds, the caller's Holder unlockTime is at least as large as it was before the Collect call.
After a call to Collect, the sum of balances plus contract balance equals the total ether received.
After Collect is called, the caller's balance after the call is always at least the caller's balance before the call.
After any call to Collect, for every address that has ever called Put, its unlockTime is never less than the block timestamp at the time of the latest Put call that increased it.
After a call to Collect, the caller's balance in the Acc mapping is always less than the total deposited amount if the unlockTime was not updated.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's Acc balance is reduced exactly by the requested amount.
After any sequence of actions ending with a call to Collect(uint256), the call always reverts (returns false) regardless of the lock time, balance, or minimum sum.
After any sequence of public calls that does not revert, the balance of msg.sender in Acc is non-negative at any time.
After a successful call to Collect(uint256 _am), the balance of msg.sender in the Acc mapping strictly decreases by exactly _am.
After calling Collect with any parameters, the caller's balance in Acc is unchanged when the call reverts.

After a successful Collect(uint256) call, the caller's balance in Acc decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn, and the call does not revert when balance >= MinSum and balance >= amount and time > unlockTime.
After Collect reduces the user balance by the amount, the new balance equals old balance minus amount.
After Collect succeeds, the user's balance in the contract decreases by the amount (i.e., new balance = old balance - amount).
After a successful Collect, the contract's MinSum does not increase.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's total balance (address(this).balance) decreases by exactly the collected amount.
After a successful Collect call where the user's balance minus the withdrawn amount would underflow, the transaction reverts.
The Collect function should only succeed if the caller's balance is at least MinSum and _am and the unlock time has passed.
After any sequence of operations ending with Collect, the caller's balance in Acc should not decrease below zero or underflow.
After Collect reverts, the caller's locked balance in Acc remains unchanged (no subtraction occurs).

The balance of msg.sender in Acc after a successful Collect call should increase by _am when the call is successful, but in the buggy version it decreases by _am and then the caller may receive the ether, causing a double subtraction.
After Collect reverts, the caller's locked balance in Acc must remain unchanged
If MinSum > 0, then a user with balance < MinSum can never successfully collect
After any sequence of actions, if a user's balance is exactly equal to MinSum, then calling Collect with an amount equal to that balance should not revert (i.e., should succeed).
When a user's balance equals exactly MinSum, the user should be able to collect an amount equal to that balance if the unlock time has passed.
If the caller's balance equals MinSum and the unlock time has passed, Collect should succeed when the amount equals the balance (since balance >= MinSum and balance >= amount).
When the user's balance equals MinSum and also equals the requested withdrawal amount, and the unlock time has passed, Collect should not revert.
